summary: This standards-track RFC defines how to advertise one or more S-BFD Discriminators using the IS-IS Router CAPABILITY TLV.

plainLanguage.summary: Routers announce their S-BFD identification numbers through IS-IS so others know where to send checks.

questions: how does is-is flood s-bfd discriminators
subtitle: A new IS-IS sub-TLV lets routers announce the S-BFD discriminators they have reserved.

tldr.problem: Seamless BFD needs every node to know the BFD discriminators that other nodes have reserved for it, so there must be a way to distribute them.
tldr.mechanism: A new sub-TLV, type 20, carried in the IS-IS Router CAPABILITY TLV, lists one or more 4-octet S-BFD discriminators.
tldr.outcome: Routers can flood their discriminators within an area or the whole domain, and IANA registered the sub-TLV value 20.

today: RFC 7883 is a Proposed Standard. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Advertise Discriminators
sections.content: RFC 7880 defines a simplified way of using Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD, RFC 5880), called Seamless BFD (S-BFD). It depends on network nodes knowing the BFD discriminators that each node has reserved for this purpose. The Intermediate System to Intermediate System (IS-IS) protocol is one possible way to advertise them.
sections.plainLanguage: To check on a friend, you need to know their special number first. IS-IS is a way to share those numbers.

sections.title: The S-BFD Discriminators Sub-TLV
sections.content:
The IS-IS Router CAPABILITY TLV from RFC 4971 carries a new sub-TLV, formatted as specified in RFC 5305. It has a Type of 20 (1 octet), a Length that is a multiple of 4 (1 octet), and then the discriminator values, 4 octets per discriminator.

Including the sub-TLV in a Router CAPABILITY TLV is optional, and an IS MAY advertise several of them. How a discriminator maps to a specific use case is out of scope.
sections.plainLanguage: It is a small labeled box: a type, a size, then a list of numbers, four bytes each.

sections.title: Flooding Scope
sections.content: Advertisements MAY be flooded within an area or throughout the domain, using the procedures in RFC 4971. The right scope depends on the intended use of S-BFD. If S-BFD will be used only within a Level-1 area, area scope is appropriate. If it will span different Level-1 areas, domain scope is appropriate.
sections.plainLanguage: Share the numbers only with your neighborhood if that is all you need, or with the whole town if you need to reach across.

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content:
IANA added value 20, S-BFD Discriminators, to the Sub-TLVs for TLV 242 registry.

The sub-TLV introduces no new risks for IS-IS, whose security is covered by ISO 10589, RFC 5304 and RFC 5310. Advertising discriminators does make it possible for attackers to start S-BFD sessions with the advertised information. Those vulnerabilities and their mitigations are discussed in RFC 7880.
sections.plainLanguage: The new number was added to the official list. Sharing the numbers lets a bad guy try to use them, and another RFC explains how to defend.
